output.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS churned_customers
FROM marts.fct_orders o
WHERE o.is_revenue
  AND o.order_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND o.order_date < DATE '2025-01-01'
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM marts.fct_orders o2
    WHERE o2.customer_id = o.customer_id
      AND o2.is_revenue
      AND o2.order_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o2.order_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
  )
output.explanation: The query counts the separate customers who had at least one completed order in 2024 and no completed order in 2025. An order counts as completed when is_revenue is true. Cancelled, returned and open orders are left out, so a customer whose only 2025 orders were cancelled or still open is still counted. The result is one number, churned_customers.
